screening_decisions.reason: This is a review article summarizing literature on drug-induced liver injury causes and mechanisms. It is not a randomized controlled trial of paracetamol for migraine treatment.

This study investigates aspirin absorption during migraine attacks, not paracetamol. The intervention is effervescent aspirin, which does not meet the selection criteria requiring paracetamol as the intervention.
This is an epidemiological analysis of paracetamol sales trends and their relationship to overdose and suicide rates. It is not a randomized controlled trial treating migraine episodes.
This is a Cochrane systematic review about aspirin for migraine, not paracetamol. The intervention studied is aspirin, which does not meet the selection criteria.

This appears to be a randomized controlled trial comparing DHE+paracetamol combination vs individual drugs (including paracetamol alone) vs placebo in 288 patients with migraine. Paracetamol is used as a treatment arm for acute migraine episodes. The study design likely meets criteria (randomized, controlled, paracetamol intervention, adequate sample size).
This is a population-based door-to-door survey assessing headache prevalence in China. It is not a randomized controlled trial of any intervention for migraine treatment.
This is a methodological study about assessing quality of RCT reports and the impact of rater blinding. It is not a clinical trial of paracetamol for migraine.
This is a methodological paper discussing statistical approaches for meta-analyses of cross-over trials. It is not a primary clinical trial of paracetamol for migraine.

This is a systematic review/meta-analysis of various pharmacological treatments for migraine. While it may include paracetamol studies, this publication itself is not a primary RCT meeting the selection criteria.
This is a telephone survey assessing headache and migraine prevalence in Germany. It is not a randomized controlled trial of any intervention.
This is a population-based prevalence study using National Health Interview Survey data. It is not a randomized controlled trial of paracetamol for migraine treatment.

This is a multicentre, randomized, double-blind, single-dose, placebo-controlled parallel group study (n=1743) comparing a fixed combination of ASA+paracetamol+caffeine vs single substances including paracetamol alone (500mg), vs placebo. Patients treated episodic tension-type headache or migraine attacks. Paracetamol is used as both a component of the combination and as a monotherapy arm for migraine treatment.
This is a review article discussing the pharmacological mechanism of action of paracetamol. It is not a randomized controlled trial of paracetamol for migraine treatment.
This is a methodological chapter from a handbook about assessing risk of bias in clinical trials. It is not a primary clinical trial of paracetamol for migraine.
This describes the creation of a database of RCTs in pain research. It is a methodological paper about database development, not a clinical trial of paracetamol for migraine.

This is a randomized, double-blind, three-way cross-over study of 46 patients comparing 1g paracetamol plus domperidone (30mg or 20mg) vs paracetamol plus placebo. Paracetamol is self-administered at onset of headache for migraine treatment. Meets criteria: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, paracetamol intervention, >10 participants per arm.
This is a statistical methods paper describing calculation of confidence intervals for various statistics. It is not a clinical trial of paracetamol for migraine.
This is a methodological study analyzing VAS scores from analgesic trials to determine what constitutes moderate pain. It is not a primary RCT of paracetamol for migraine treatment.

This is a randomized, double-blind, crossover, multicenter, phase III clinical trial of 229 adult patients comparing etodolac (400mg and 800mg) vs 1000mg paracetamol for acute migraine treatment. Paracetamol is self-administered at onset of migraine attacks. Meets criteria: randomized, double-blind, active-controlled, paracetamol intervention, >10 participants per arm.
This study examines aspirin absorption during migraine attacks with and without metoclopramide. The intervention is effervescent aspirin, not paracetamol. Does not meet selection criteria.
This is a literature review about paracetamol poisoning and pack size legislation, not a clinical trial evaluating paracetamol for migraine treatment. Wrong study type and wrong outcome focus.

Randomised crossover trial comparing Domperamol (fixed combination of domperidone and paracetamol) with sumatriptan for moderate to severe migraine. 120 patients recruited from 23 primary care practices. Meets criteria: randomised, uses paracetamol (in combination), treats migraine, adequate sample size (>10 per arm).
Case series of 14 patients receiving intravenous metoclopramide exclusively with no other analgesic drug. No paracetamol intervention. Also not randomised or controlled.
Methodological paper discussing meta-analysis techniques and guidelines. Not a clinical trial evaluating paracetamol for migraine.
Cross-sectional economic survey estimating costs of headache disorders in Europe. Not a clinical trial evaluating paracetamol for migraine treatment.

Double-blind, three-way crossover trial comparing isometheptene/acetaminophen/dichloralphenazone combination with acetaminophen alone and placebo in 56 adult migraineurs (40 female, 16 male). Each subject evaluated medication effectiveness in 6 headache episodes. Meets criteria: randomised, double-blind, includes acetaminophen (paracetamol) arm, treats migraine, adequate sample size.
Epidemiological survey study describing patterns of medical treatment for migraineurs in the US. Not a randomised controlled trial evaluating paracetamol efficacy.
Basic science/mechanism of action study about paracetamol's antipyretic activity via prostaglandin synthetase inhibition. Not a clinical trial for migraine treatment.
Pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic study in 5 healthy volunteers assessing COX inhibition. Not a clinical trial evaluating paracetamol for migraine treatment. Sample size too small and wrong population.
Review article about migraine underdiagnosis and diagnostic challenges. Not a clinical trial evaluating paracetamol for migraine treatment.
Review/commentary article about COX-3 and paracetamol mechanism of action. Not a clinical trial evaluating paracetamol for migraine treatment.
Methodological paper about NNT calculation. Abstract describes fungal infection research (Rhizopus/Pseudomonas), completely unrelated to paracetamol or migraine.
Epidemiological burden of disease study quantifying YLDs globally. Not a clinical trial evaluating paracetamol for migraine treatment.

Randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind clinical trial of acetaminophen 1000mg for episodic migraine headache. 346 outpatient adults enrolled (177 acetaminophen, 169 placebo). Primary outcomes include pain reduction at 2 hours. Clearly meets all criteria: randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, self-administered paracetamol, treats migraine, adequate sample size.
Systematic review about paracetamol safety in alcoholic patients, not specifically about migraine treatment. Focus is on hepatic injury risk, not migraine efficacy. Wrong outcome focus.
Telephone survey study about patient preferences and priorities for migraine therapy. Not a randomised controlled trial evaluating paracetamol efficacy.
Editorial/commentary about Global Burden of Disease Survey findings. Not a clinical trial evaluating paracetamol for migraine treatment.
Methodological case study about duplicate publication impact on meta-analysis, using ondansetron for postoperative emesis as example. Not about paracetamol or migraine.
Review/opinion piece about paracetamol hepatotoxicity and therapeutic misadventure. Not a clinical trial evaluating paracetamol for migraine treatment.

Randomized, double-blind trial comparing IV metoclopramide with subcutaneous sumatriptan for migraine in emergency department. No paracetamol intervention included. Does not meet criteria as paracetamol is not used.
This is an epidemiological survey study estimating prevalence of headache disorders in Russia. It is not a randomized controlled trial and does not test paracetamol treatment for migraine.
This is a systematic review of epidemiological studies on headache prevalence in Europe. It is not a primary randomized controlled trial and does not test paracetamol treatment.

This is a randomized, double-blind, active-controlled crossover study comparing tolfenamic acid with paracetamol (500mg and 1000mg) for treating migraine attacks. 83 patients were enrolled with 4 treatment arms, meeting the minimum 10 participants per arm requirement. Paracetamol was self-administered to treat acute migraine episodes.

This is a longitudinal survey study evaluating economic burden and healthcare resource utilization in transformed migraine. It is not a randomized controlled trial and does not test paracetamol treatment.
This is a clinical practice guideline document providing expert recommendations for migraine treatment. It is not a primary randomized controlled trial.
This is an overview paper discussing epidemiological evidence and disability measurement for migraine. It is not a randomized controlled trial and does not test paracetamol treatment.

This is a before-and-after observational study evaluating the impact of legislation on paracetamol poisoning rates. It is not a randomized controlled trial and does not test paracetamol for migraine treatment.

This is a double-blind controlled study testing Paramax (paracetamol 0.5g + metoclopramide 5mg) versus placebo for acute migraine treatment. 49 patients were enrolled, which should provide at least 10 participants per treatment arm. This fits the review topic of paracetamol with an antiemetic for migraine.
This is a literature review and recommendations paper on OTC drugs for migraine. It is not a primary randomized controlled trial.
This is a basic science study describing the cloning and structure of COX-3 enzyme. It is not a clinical trial and does not test paracetamol treatment for migraine in humans.

This is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial with 173 patients across 4 treatment arms (rizatriptan+acetaminophen, rizatriptan alone, acetaminophen alone, placebo). Each arm would have approximately 43 patients, exceeding the 10 participant minimum. Acetaminophen was self-administered to treat acute migraine attacks.
This is a methodological paper discussing trial size requirements and statistical power. It is not a primary randomized controlled trial testing paracetamol for migraine.
This is a population-based survey study evaluating disability and treatment patterns in chronic migraine. It is not a randomized controlled trial and does not test paracetamol treatment.
This is a review article discussing the economic burden and disease management of migraine. It is not a primary randomized controlled trial.
This is a clinical practice guide providing recommendations for migraine management. It is not a primary randomized controlled trial.
This is a basic science review discussing the mechanism of action of acetaminophen. It is not a clinical trial testing paracetamol for migraine treatment.
This is an epidemiological survey study assessing migraine prevalence and preventive therapy use in the US population. It is not a randomized controlled trial and does not test paracetamol treatment.
This is a population-based survey study evaluating migraine recognition and treatment patterns in France. It is not a randomized controlled trial and does not test paracetamol treatment.

This is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study comparing oral acetaminophen 1000mg with placebo for treating acute migraine attacks. The study was population-based and tested self-administered paracetamol for migraine. The sample size appears adequate with at least 10 participants per treatment arm.

This is an economic analysis study using cross-sectional survey data to evaluate healthcare costs in migraine patients across European countries. It is not a randomized controlled trial and does not test paracetamol treatment.

This study investigates aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid/ASA) pharmacokinetics in migraine patients, not paracetamol (acetaminophen). The selection criteria explicitly require studies using self-administered paracetamol to treat migraine headache episodes. While the study is randomized and involves migraine patients with adequate sample size (30 patients across 3 treatment groups), the intervention drug is fundamentally different from what the review protocol specifies. Aspirin and paracetamol are distinct analgesic medications with different mechanisms of action. Therefore, this study does not meet the intervention criterion and must be excluded.
